title: High-Performing Teams & Individual Contribution
summary: Examine the habits of effective teams and learn how to identify, document, and improve your own contribution within shared work.
objectives: Distinguish team success from proof of individual contribution.
Evaluate personal contribution using specific actions and results.

vocab.def: The specific work, decision, support, or result a person adds to a team effort.
How effectively a team works together to achieve its intended result.
Identifying which person, action, or source is responsible for a particular contribution or result.
Ongoing effort to learn from results and make future teamwork more effective.

sections.heading: High-performing teams make the work visible
sections.body: Strong teams understand goals, responsibilities, dependencies, status, and next steps. They do not rely entirely on assumptions or informal memory.

sections.heading: Effective teams combine different strengths
sections.body: Team members may contribute different skills, experiences, perspectives, and responsibilities. Good collaboration uses those differences to strengthen the shared result.

sections.heading: Team success does not prove individual contribution
sections.body: A successful team outcome shows that the team achieved something. It does not automatically show what each individual did. Individual contribution should be identified through specific actions, work, or evidence.

sections.heading: Teams improve by reviewing how they worked
sections.body: After a project, teams can examine what worked, what caused delays or confusion, what should change, and what practices should be repeated next time.

practice.prompt: A team completes a successful project. How could you describe your own contribution responsibly?
practice.answer: Identify the specific tasks, decisions, communication, or results that you personally completed rather than claiming the team's entire result.

practice.prompt: What should a team discuss after finishing an important project?
practice.answer: What worked, what did not, where coordination broke down, what should change, and which practices should be repeated.

quiz.question: Which statement about individual contribution is most accurate?
options: Team membership alone does not prove what an individual contributed
Every team member should receive credit for every part of the work
Only the team leader has an individual contribution
Individual contribution does not matter when the team succeeds
quiz.answer: Team membership alone does not prove what an individual contributed

lab.objective: Review a simulated team project and create an individual contribution statement that distinguishes personal work from the team's overall result.

reflectionPrompt: Why is it important to distinguish your own contribution from the overall success of a team?
